definition: A condition where part or all of your lung deflates or collapses due to air sacs (alveoli) losing air.
general_symptoms: Blue or gray skin, lips or nails (cyanosis)
general_causes: Being in bed sick and not taking deep breaths, especially when mucus accumulates in your airways
Anesthesia during surgery (not breathing deeply enough or coughing to clear mucus)
Taking shallow breaths due to chest pain
Lying in bed with belly pushing up against lungs
Buildup of mucus in airways (mucus plug) after surgery, during severe asthma attacks, or due to infection
Breathing in a foreign object (food, small toy parts)
Underlying illnesses (COPD, bronchiectasis, ARDS, COVID-19, pneumonia)
general_treatments: Monitoring/regular appointments (mild cases often go away without treatment)
Chemotherapy or radiation therapy (to treat a tumor)
Walking around, breathing exercises (especially for post-surgery)
general_outlook: Often goes away on its own
In most cases, with proper diagnosis and treatment, outlook is good
Often reversible once cause is determined
Recovery is usually quick without serious lasting effects
Atelectasis after surgery usually goes away after 24 hours
Further treatment may be needed if caused by a long-lasting condition

subtypes_and_causes.mechanism: Something around the lung pushes against it causing it to collapse.
A blockage prevents air from filling alveoli; air enters bloodstream without new air coming in, causing alveoli to collapse.
Lack of surfactant (layer of lipids and proteins lining alveoli that protect lungs from collapsing).

subtypes_and_causes.definition: Partial collapse of the lower part of the lungs.
causes: Being in bed and having belly push up on lungs

subtypes_and_causes.definition: The pleura folds and causes lung to collapse.
Gravity causes the lowest parts of lungs to deflate.
Mildest form of atelectasis; usually doesn't cause symptoms and goes away quickly.
